user.title: Train Commute Companion
user.description: Enter your NS API key. Next you pick your stations and times.

data_description.api_key: Your NS API key from the NS API portal.

data.name: Profile name
data.require_accessible: Ask NS for accessible journeys (assistance can require booking)

data.return_time: Return first train (HH:MM), optional in window mode
data.outbound_transfers: Outbound transfer stations, in travel order
data.return_transfers: Return transfer stations, in travel order
data.outbound_buffer: Minutes from your door to the outbound platform
data.return_buffer: Minutes from your door to the return platform
data.outbound_pick: Outbound train choice in window mode

data.return_pick: Return train choice in window mode
data.return_min_stay: Return minimum stay in minutes, 0 for none

data_description.outbound_active_lead: Leave blank for travel buffer plus 15 minutes. Ends quiet early watch; must be at least your travel buffer.
data_description.return_active_lead: Leave blank for travel buffer plus 15 minutes. Ends quiet early watch; must be at least your travel buffer.
data_description.outbound_mode: Fixed follows your usual train. Window follows the earliest good train between the two window times.
data_description.outbound_window_start: In window mode this is the earliest departure. In fixed mode it is when watching starts. Leave both blank in fixed mode for the default.
data_description.outbound_window_end: In window mode this is the latest departure. It is always needed in window mode.
data_description.outbound_pick: Pick the train when I leave follows no train until you leave. Then it takes the next train you can catch. Without location it uses the earliest train with silent misses.
data_description.outbound_min_stay: Window mode only. The window starts no earlier than your arrival on the other trip plus this many minutes. For example 480 for 8 hours at work.
data_description.return_mode: Fixed follows your usual train. Window follows the earliest good train between the two window times.
data_description.return_window_start: In window mode this is the earliest departure. In fixed mode it is when watching starts. Leave both blank in fixed mode for the default.
data_description.return_window_end: In window mode this is the latest departure. It is always needed in window mode.
data_description.return_pick: Pick the train when I leave follows no train until you leave. Then it takes the next train you can catch. Without location it uses the earliest train with silent misses.
data_description.return_min_stay: Window mode only. The window starts no earlier than your arrival on the other trip plus this many minutes. For example 480 for 8 hours at work.

profile_details.title: Transfer time and holidays

data.edit_weekday_times: Set different departure times by weekday
data.compensation_reminder: Remind me to check NS compensation after a confirmed delay
data.quiet_repeat_misses: Silent missed-train message after the first one of the day
data.delay_step_min: Delay change for another update in minutes
data.edit_day_overrides: Set a different mode, window, train choice or stay for some days
data.other_station_dwell_min: Minutes at another station before it counts
data.ask_to_remember_station: Offer to remember a new boarding station
data.weather: Weather forecasts, practical tips and KNMI warnings

data_description.delay_min: Default 3. Whole minutes from 1 to 1440. Before the active point, the minimum is at least 5. Cancellations, transfers and arrival-limit warnings stay enabled.
data_description.delay_step_min: Default 3. Whole minutes from 1 to 1440, measured from the last stated delay in either direction. Recovery to 1 minute or less still counts.
data_description.custom_timetable_horizon: On by default. Turn off to use up to three commute dates within ten calendar days.
data_description.timetable_horizon_unit: Count calendar days from tomorrow or count only upcoming dates with a fixed journey.
data_description.timetable_horizon_count: Enter a whole number from 1 to 14. The default is seven.
data_description.leave_by: Show when to leave in check-in and pre-trip advice, and in the status sensor. Uses your travel buffer. Enabled by default.
data_description.compensation_reminder: Optional saved-plan comparison after you explicitly confirm arrival. Uses routine notification routing and category controls. This does not determine claim eligibility.
data_description.quiet_repeat_misses: When you stay at home or work past several trains, only the first "you missed" makes a sound. The later ones still arrive, silently.
data_description.outbound_other_stations: TCC follows a train from these stations by itself when your phone is there and no train is followed yet.
data_description.return_other_stations: TCC follows a train from these stations by itself when your phone is there and no train is followed yet.
data_description.other_station_radius_m: How near your phone must be to a station. Default 500.
data_description.other_station_dwell_min: 0 means one location fix is enough. Default 0.
data_description.ask_to_remember_station: After you say Yes at a new station, TCC asks once whether to remember it.
data_description.weather: On by default. Uses station coordinates, never phone location. Forecasts need no key. Official warnings need your own KNMI key under Configure > Weather.

validate.title: Check the profiles file
validate.description:
{report}

Phone location is not always reliable. In stations, tunnels, or with battery saving on, your position can be late or wrong. Location only helps the companion. It never hides a warning about your train.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Changing the phone or the alert style sends the test notifications again.

data_description.profiles_path: Full path to your profiles file. Copy the starter file there first.
data_description.notify_service: The phone that gets the alerts. Both test notifications go to it.
data_description.loud_style: How a loud alert arrives. Quiet updates are always silent.
data_description.notifications_enabled_entity: Optional. Off pauses phone notifications and alert events. Relevant alerts wait without a failed delivery. Missing or unknown states leave notifications enabled.
data_description.notifications_quiet_entity: Optional. On makes phone notifications silent. Alert events keep their original severity. Missing or unknown states use the selected alert style.

test.title: Did both arrive?
test.description: A loud and a silent test notification were sent to notify.{service}.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Every alert is also sent as signed JSON to these URLs. Saving a change first sends each URL a signed loud and a signed silent test, which it must accept. Your phone stays the proof that alerts arrive.

data_description.webhook_urls: One URL per line. Leave empty to turn webhooks off.
data_description.webhook_secret: At least 16 characters. Give the same secret to the receiver.
data_description.webhook_token: Optional. Only for receivers that want a token, such as OpenClaw. Sent to every URL.
